'''''Tabernaemontana divaricata''''', commonly called '''pinwheel flower''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=TADI5|taxon=Tabernaemontana divaricata|accessdate=7 December 2015}}</ref> '''crape jasmine''', '''Ceylon jasmine''', '''East India rosebay''', and '''Nero's crown''',<ref>''Medicinal Plants of India and Pakistan'', Dastur J.F., pub.1962 by D.P. Taraporevala Sons and Co. Private Ltd., Mumbai, 4th Indian reprint 1977{{page needed|date=December 2016}}</ref> is an [[evergreen]] shrub or small tree native to South Asia, Southeast Asia and China.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /> In zones where it is not hardy it is grown as a house/glasshouse plant for its attractive flowers and foliage. The [[Plant stem|stem]] exudes a milky latex when broken, whence comes the name '''milk flower'''.

==Description==
The plant generally grows to a height of {{convert|5|-|6|ft|m|1|order=flip}} and is [[dichotomous branching|dichotomously]] branched. The large shiny leaves are deep green and about {{convert|6|in|cm|0|order=flip|abbr=on}} in length and {{convert|2|in|cm|0|order=flip|abbr=on}} in width. The waxy blossoms are found in small clusters on the stem tips. The (single) flowers have the characteristic 'pinwheel' shape also seen in other [[genera]] in the family Apocynaceae such as ''[[Vinca]]'' and ''[[Nerium]]''. Both single and [[double-flowered]] forms are cultivated, the flowers of both forms being white. The plant blooms in spring but flowers appear sporadically all year. The flowers have a pleasing fragrance.<ref>''The Royal Horticultural Society Dictionary of Gardening'' ed. Chittenden, Fred J. 2nd ed. by Synge, Patrick M. Volume IV : Pt-Zy, p.2074 (as T. coronaria). Pub. Oxford at the Clarendon Press 1965. Reprinted 1984. {{ISBN|0-19-869106-8}}</ref> More than 66 [[alkaloid]]s are found in the shrub.<ref>{{Cite book | title = Medicinal Plants of East and Southeast Asia: Attributed Properties and Uses | author = Perry, Lily M. | publisher = MIT Press | date = 1980 | isbn = 978-0-262-16076-6 | url-access = registration | url = https://archive.org/details/MedicinalP_00_Perr }}{{page needed|date=December 2016}}</ref> Its habitats include montane brushwoods and sparse forests.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tabernaemontana divaricata in Flora of China @ efloras.org |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=210002194 |access-date=2022-09-27 |website=www.efloras.org}}</ref>

== Phytochemistry ==
The species is known to produce many [[alkaloids]] including [[catharanthine]], [[conolidine]], [[coronaridine]], [[dregamine]], [[ibogamine]], [[tabersonine]], [[voacangine]], [[voacamine]] and [[voacristine]].<ref name="pmid17191876">{{cite journal |vauthors=Kam TS, Pang HS, Choo YM, Komiyama K |title=Biologically active ibogan and vallesamine derivatives from ''Tabernaemontana divaricata'' |journal=Chemistry and Biodiversity |volume=1 |issue=4 |pages=646–56 |date=April 2004 |pmid=17191876 |doi=10.1002/cbdv.200490056 |s2cid=12805328 |url= |issn=}}</ref> [[Ibogaine]] may occur in multiple ''[[Tabernaemontana]]'' species.<ref name="pmid17191876"/>
